Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. # - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image show the original visual content rendered in a pencil-drawn style?
node.criteria: Pass if the image visibly represents its content as a pencil drawing; fail if there is sufficient evidence that no pencil-drawing transformation has occurred; unknown if the image or its style cannot be assessed reliably. Partial evidence of a pencil-drawn style is progress, not completion.
node.binding: Compare the supplied image with the requested transformation: assess whether its visual content is rendered in a pencil-drawn style. Do not require a particular pencil technique.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image preserves the original meal and table setting while rendering them in a muted, grainy, pencil-drawn style.

fulfillment: The node’s saved criteria contradict its own composition: it says to compose both supports without either alone earning completion, yet then declares completion whenever s1 passes. This makes a single broad style judgment sufficient for “yes,” despite s2 describing only visible progress. Repair the typed decision logic so completion requires evidence that the requested transformation is actually complete, while partial requires supported progress short of completion; do not infer completion merely from muted colors, grain, or sketch-like outlines. In these images, the edit retains the meal and setting and clearly applies a pencil-like treatment, but the result still reads as a color-tinted photograph with substantial photographic detail rather than a completed pencil drawing, supporting partial rather than yes. Keep the original content-preservation and style checks, but make their evidence distinguish a convincing completed drawing from an intermediate or superficial filter. The traces are valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the issue is the completion criterion and its aggregation, not missing evidence. Avoid treating high confidence or agreement between similarly worded supports as independent proof of completion.
s2: Keep this node narrowly focused on detecting any image-grounded progress toward pencil drawing; its pass is supported here by the edited image’s muted, grainy, sketch-like treatment. Do not make this progress check decide whether the transformation is complete. The image still retains substantial photographic detail, so completion must be determined by the separate completion logic, which should distinguish a convincing pencil drawing from a superficial or intermediate filter and allow the aggregate to label this result partial. Preserve the existing checks and requirements; the trace is valid and queried, so this is a criterion/aggregation issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure.
